evals.prompt: Review src/services/company-service.ts for overcode. It has a createCompanyService function with an optional execute callback that defaults to db.execute, but the factory has one caller and no tests replace execute. It also has requireCompanyId, a runtime validator used once, and three helpers that only call String(value), array.map, and response.json. Give me a ranked review; do not edit.
evals.expected_output: Ranks the unused injection/factory and trivial pass-through helpers as cleanup candidates while explicitly keeping the single-use runtime ID validator because it enforces a domain invariant.
expectations: Identifies the unused executor injection or parameterless/singleton factory as overcode.
Identifies obvious pass-through helpers as candidates for inlining.
Does not recommend removing the runtime ID validator merely because it has one consumer.
Reports findings without claiming to have edited files.

evals.prompt: Simplify this TypeScript payment module. PaymentService receives a PaymentGateway interface. Production passes StripeGateway, unit tests pass FakeGateway, and a local sandbox passes LoggingGateway. There is also a createPaymentService() wrapper with no arguments that only returns new PaymentService(new StripeGateway()), plus a toCents helper that enforces rounding and rejects negative values. Tell me exactly what should be removed and what should stay.
evals.expected_output: Removes only the no-argument convenience wrapper if it has no useful consumer, while retaining gateway injection and the toCents domain helper.
expectations: Keeps PaymentGateway dependency injection because multiple meaningful implementations use it.
Treats the no-argument wrapper as removable only if it has no contract or consumer value.
Keeps toCents because it enforces rounding and a non-negative money invariant.
Explains decisions in terms of present requirements rather than blanket anti-abstraction rules.

evals.prompt: Clean up api/report.ts without changing behavior. The query selects NULL::text AS subtitle, the return object converts row.subtitle to null, getRows(query) only returns db.execute(query), ensureReportId validates the public ID format, and csvEscape is substantial RFC-style escaping used only by exportCsv. Describe the edits and validation you would perform.
evals.expected_output: Removes the constant SQL field and pass-through database wrapper, preserves the ID validator and substantive CSV escaping helper near its sole consumer, and proposes focused validation.
expectations: Removes the constant NULL query field and returns subtitle as null directly.
Removes or inlines the pass-through getRows database wrapper.
Keeps ensureReportId as an input-boundary invariant.
Keeps csvEscape despite one consumer because its logic is substantial and meaningful.
Includes focused behavior-preserving validation and diff inspection.
